gitCommit.body:
Record the 2026-09-14 session-3 day and rebuild tomorrow's agenda (#329)

Docs only, CLAUDE.md. Closes out #326 (cron observability), #327 (the
field_updated_at time-diff fix) and #328 (the GrabExpress change
analysis) — all merged, deployed and prod-verified.

Records what is worth not re-deriving rather than a list of what was
done.

From #326, the part that generalises: /admin/crons is the screen we open
to answer "what would this look like if it were silently doing nothing?"
and it was itself silently doing nothing for 47 of 59 jobs while actively
lying about the other 12, because it coloured by whether a timestamp
existed rather than whether it was timely. A five-minute cron three days
dead rendered green. The refinement now written down: ask of any status
surface what it renders for a thing that died three days ago; if the
answer is green, it is decoration.

Also records the verification taken 45 minutes after deploy rather than
the one taken two minutes after, which proved nothing — 28 distinct
crons, 134 rows, zero errors, every short-interval job under its own
name. And the near-miss: at two minutes post-deploy the evidence matched
my own written failure signal, and the honest reading was that it could
not distinguish a broken wrapper from one that had not ticked yet. A
signal about a scheduled job has to be expressed in that job's own
cadence.

From #328, the finding that sets the build order: the checkout price rule
exists twice, once as a pure tested function and once re-implemented by
hand in the page, with nothing asserting they agree and a silent failure
mode if only one is edited. Plus the honest pre-existing risk that
shippingFee is client-supplied and never recomputed server-side, bounded
today only because a fixed fee caps the live quote away.

Tomorrow's agenda is rebuilt around what does NOT wait on Grab, since the
stall threshold and the serviceType question are held until onboarding.
The two unblocked steps are the ones that make a later carrier an
admin/ops job rather than a money-path edit. Auto re-routing is recorded
as decided out with the door left open, not as an omission.

Carries two of my own corrections, both fixed by measuring rather than
re-reading: the source/test split was backwards on first pass, and the
carrier name lives in three places rather than two.
